messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug pertains to the handling of unrecognized long options and tokens when parsing command-line arguments using the PosixParser with stopAtNonOption enabled. The main parse method in Parser (likely PosixParser inherits or overrides it) calls flatten, which processes all tokens before actual parsing.

In PosixParser's flatten method, when a token begins with "--" and contains '=', it splits the token into two tokens around '='. Thus, "--zop==1" becomes "--zop" and "=1". There is no check to see if "--zop" is a recognized option before this splitting and token bursting. This causes non-recognized long options to be split and the parser to continue processing tokens as if they were options or arguments.

In the parse method, when stopAtNonOption is true, if a token starts with "-" but is not recognized (getOptions().hasOption(t) returns false), the parser sets eatTheRest = true and adds the token as an argument (cmd.addArg(t)), but continues processing all subsequent tokens. This leads to the tokens after a non-recognized long option being "burst" and split (due to flatten) instead of treated as normal arguments.

The burstToken method further processes tokens that are not recognized single-character options. It splits such tokens into individual options. If any individual option is unrecognized and stopAtNonOption is true, it breaks out of bursting and processes the remaining token substring as arguments, but the original "=" splitting and token splitting in flatten still happens for long tokens starting with "--".

The current test:
- passes the args: "--zop==1", "-abtoast", "--b=bar" with some options 'a' and 'b' recognized.
- expects after parsing with stopAtNonOption == true that all tokens after the unrecognized "--zop" are treated as arguments, resulting in 3 extra args.
- the bug is that tokens after "--zop" are incorrectly parsed and split, not preserved as arguments intact.

The recent bug reports also talk about similar issues where PosixParser fails to stop bursting tokens after an unrecognized option or stops only on a certain character but continues bursting tokens even though stopAtNonOption is true.

In summary, the problem stems from PosixParser's flatten method splitting and bursting tokens too aggressively for unrecognized long options before the parser has a chance to stop processing on non-options tokens when stopAtNonOption is true. The code needs to be corrected to ensure that unrecognized long options are not split/burst and that processing stops immediately after encountering them when stopAtNonOption is true.

This explains why the test expecting 3 arguments in cl.getArgList() fails because the parser continues processing and splitting tokens beyond the unrecognized long option.

Thus, the bug occurs due to the logic in PosixParser.flatten (handling splitting using '=' and bursting tokens) and the parse method's handling of stopAtNonOption flag for unrecognized long options.
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.flatten(org.apache.commons.cli.Options,java.lang.String[],boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.Parser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options,java.lang.String[],java.util.Properties,boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.burstToken(java.lang.String,boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
